title: LLMs-as-Judges: A Comprehensive Survey on LLM-based Evaluation Methods

bias_targets.methodology: Swapping the order of candidate answers and evaluating the consistency of the LLM's judgments (swap-based debiasing methods).
Using automated perturbations and controlled modifications to quantify the impact of response length on LLM judgments.
Assessing whether models disproportionately favor responses containing references to authoritative sources, books, or experts, regardless of factual accuracy.
Evaluating whether models inappropriately align their judgments with a presented majority opinion or consensus.
Measuring shifts in evaluation outcomes when model names, identifiers, or contextual cues are anonymized or removed.
Assessing judgment shifts based on identity-related markers included in the text, such as gender, ethnicity, religion, or other social categorizations.
Evaluating whether models disproportionately reward responses that exhibit specific emotional tones (e.g., cheerful or optimistic) while penalizing negative or intense ones.
Analyzing if LLMs inherently favor more frequently occurring tokens from their pre-training data over less common ones during the evaluation process.
Evaluating whether judgments are skewed or rendered culturally insensitive based on the specific cultural contexts, domains, or few-shot examples provided.
Using simulated annotator preferences or adversarial debate mechanisms to identify inflated confidence and overly assertive but incorrect evaluations.
Comparing a model's evaluation scores on its own generated outputs versus the outputs generated by other LLMs.
Assessing whether models assign higher scores to responses that include a revision history or explicit refinement process, regardless of actual quality improvement.
Introducing irrelevant or unimportant details (e.g., meaningless statements) into the input to test if the model's evaluation outcomes are altered.
Presenting answers containing logical errors (e.g., circular reasoning, false dilemmas) to test if the evaluating model fails to identify these inconsistencies.
